The label hugs its one line instead, and the row clips it at its own edge, where the span ends too, so Figma shows what Chromium draws.

Collapsed to the icon rail at the default and sm sizes, the row's 8px end padding lies between where the label span ends and where the row clips, and the label hugs its one line past the span, so the build cannot show that the row's clip cuts the text off at the span's edge. The span starts at the row's clip edge there, with no room left after the icon and the gap, so neither Chromium nor Figma shows any of the text. At the large size the row has no end padding and clips where the span ends.

On Remove, the chip's last segment, `rounded-none` wins only the start corners, since the later `last:rounded-e-[calc(var(--radius-md)-1px)]` takes the end corners. A radius per corner maps on all four corners or none, and the end corners do not map, so `readCorners` maps no corner, and Remove takes the square fallback `mapBox` gives a box whose corners do not map, 0 on every corner. The other segments set `rounded-none` alone and map it. Remove is a transparent ghost button inside the chip's own rounded border, so its square end corners paint nothing at rest that the chip's corners do not.

Every member of a group is as long across it as the others, and fixed there: the horizontal group's Buttons each take `control-h-md` as their height, and the vertical group's Icon buttons each take `control-h-md` as their width. CSS stretches no item whose size across is fixed (CSS Flexbox 1 §9.4), so the stretch moves nothing, and the group hugs its members across as Figma draws it.

A focused item of a segmented Toggle group stacks above its neighbors, so Chromium paints its focus ring over the pressed neighbor's fill where the two meet. The neighbors are instances in the Segmented toggle group's row, and Figma paints a row's layers in their order, with no field that lifts one layer of an auto layout above the next, so the kit paints the later item over the ring there.

The item row wraps, and item-content grows beside the row's other layers with its content-based minimum. CSS breaks the line where those layers and the gaps leave the content less than that minimum (CSS Flexbox 1 §9.3 step 1), and a Figma row never wraps. Chromium sets the row on one line in every captured cell, and the build draws that one line. The capture measures one line in the cell's own mode only, and it reads a second line that a negative margin lifts over the first as one line, so no measurement proves the row never breaks.

The chips box wraps its row, and the input's `flex-1` grows beside the chips from its 64px `min-w-16`. CSS sets the input on a line at that minimum, so it breaks the line where the chips and the gaps leave it less than 64px (CSS Flexbox 1 §9.3 step 1), and a Figma row never wraps. The Apple and Cherry chips leave the input room on one line in every captured cell, and the build draws that one line. A box whose chips fill the line breaks it in Chromium and stays on one line in Figma, a #922 line.

The row gap spaces the lines the chips box's wrap makes when the input's 64px `min-w-16` breaks the line beside the chips (CSS Flexbox 1 §9.3 step 1, CSS Box Alignment 3 §8). A Figma row never wraps, so it has no second line to space. Chromium sets one line in every captured cell, where the row gap adds nothing, and the build draws that one line.

The range's field box wraps its row and grows to its lines above its `min-height`. The build drops a wrap only in a row of a fixed height, where `align-content` stretches the one line to the row's height (CSS Flexbox 1 §9.4), so this wrap stays unmapped. Chromium sets one line at the 384px sample in every mode, and the kit draws that line as a row that does not wrap.

The trigger's auto start margin sets it at the end of the field box. The box hugs its height above its `min-height` and its segment rows set `self-stretch`, so a frame around the rows and the separator would hug them where CSS stretches them to the line (PF), and the build reads no auto margin in such a row. The kit draws the trigger right after the end segment row.

Each segment row stretches across the field box's one line, which the box's `min-height` sets in every captured cell (CSS Flexbox 1 §9.4). The box hugs its height, and a Figma layer cannot fill a frame that hugs it, so each row hugs its segments and the box centers it with `items-center`. Its segments sit at the same height either way.
